passages.note: Official bill page lists Wesco as House sponsor of SB 101 (2015), Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act.
House 3rd reading roll call records Wesco's Yea vote on the single-subject SB 101.

passages.provision_quote: A person whose exercise of religion has been substantially burdened, or is likely to be substantially burdened, by a violation of this chapter may assert the violation or impending violation as a claim or defense in a judicial or administrative proceeding, regardless of whether the state or any other governmental entity is a party to the proceeding.
passages.note: Enacted text lets a person raise a substantial-burden-on-religion claim as a defense in any proceeding, a faith-based exemption route from generally applicable law.

rows.reasoning: As House sponsor, Wesco carried SB 101 (2015), Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act, to passage and voted Yea on its single-subject 3rd reading (Yea 63, Nay 31, not near-unanimous). The enacted law lets a person assert a substantially-burdened exercise of religion 'as a claim or defense in a judicial or administrative proceeding, regardless of whether the state or any other governmental entity is a party,' subject to a compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means test — matching rung 4, 'protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs,' rather than rung 5's unconditional autonomy or rung 2's guarantee that anti-discrimination protections aren't overridden.
